name: 中華そば ほそかわ 花屋町店 (Chuka Soba Hosokawa (Hanayacho))

claims.text: Single small ramen line built around wheat noodles boiled in shared water; wheat cross-contact is unavoidable.
Broth and tare are soy-sauce (shoyu) based, which is virtually always wheat-fermented; no gluten-free tare is offered.
Every bowl uses a chicken-bone, pork and back-fat broth with meat toppings; nothing on the menu is plant-based.

name: 中華そば らんたん (Chuka Soba Rantan)

claims.text: Custom wheat noodles made with whole-grain flour (全粒粉入りの特注麺) are the core of every bowl; the kitchen is a wheat-noodle ramen operation with no gluten-free handling noted.
The signature ramen is built on an aged soy sauce tare (熟成醤油 中華そば), and the tsukemen dipping sauce uses aged soy sauce (熟成醤油) — conventionally wheat-fermented.

All broths are animal-based (国産鶏・鰹・煮干 — chicken, bonito, dried sardine); the tsukemen uses 国産鴨脂 (domestic duck fat) and shellfish dashi (貝ダシ) and egg dishes appear on the menu. No vegetable broth offered.

name: 中華そば 六 (Chuka Soba Roku)

claims.text: The dish is wheat ramen noodles in a meat broth, with wheat-wrapped wontons, prepared in a small 12-seat shared kitchen; no gluten-free handling is advertised. Treat as not celiac-safe.
As a Chinese-style chuka-soba, the tare is almost certainly soy/shoyu-based, which standardly contains wheat. No wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.

The broth itself is animal-based (five bone stocks: duck, chicken, venison, beef, pork) and wontons contain pork, so there is no vegan-compatible base; cross-contact is moot because no plant-based option exists.

name: 中華そば専門店 ふくなが (Chuka Soba Senmonten Fukunaga)

claims.text: The broth is a rich soy (shoyu) tare; Japanese soy sauce of this style virtually always contains wheat. No wheat-free tare is offered.
All bowls share a pork-bone broth and the kitchen handles pork chashu, gyoza and karaage; there is no separate vegan preparation.
All vegetables and ingredients are domestically sourced, and the shop makes its own noodles in-house.

name: 中華そば専門店 なか小路 (Chuka Soba Senmonten Nakakoji)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles (from Kondo Seimen) are boiled in shared water; a celiac-safe preparation is not possible here.
The house bowl is a soy-sauce (shoyu) back-fat ramen; standard Japanese shoyu tare contains wheat, and no gluten-free tare is indicated.
Broths are chicken- and pork-based with back fat, topped with pork chashu; sides include beef tendon, karaage, and ginger pork, so no dish is free of animal products.

name: 中華そば笑麺 (Chuka Soba Shomen)

claims.text: Single small ramen kitchen built around wheat noodles boiled in shared water; no gluten-free protocol or separate prep is indicated, so cross-contact is effectively unavoidable.
The broth is finished with an aged soy-sauce (shoyu) tare; standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat, making the seasoning a wheat source.
Broth is chicken-bone based, enriched with pork back fat and served with pork chashu; no plant-based broth or toppings exist, so there is no vegan path on the menu.

name: 中華そば 双鳩 (Chuka Soba Soukyu)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles boiled in shared water, with a shoyu-based tare and chicken/pork broth — gluten is inherent to the dish and unavoidable here.
The broth is a shoyu (soy sauce) base; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, and no wheat-free tare is indicated.
Animal-based throughout — chicken-and-pork-bone broth with grilled pork topping; no vegan preparation exists.

name: 中華そば たく味 (Chuka-soba Takumi)

claims.text: Standard ramen tare for a shop of this style is made with wheat-containing soy sauce, and no gluten-free tare is indicated.
Broth is long-simmered pork bone and bowls are topped with chashu pork, so all cooking equipment and broth contact animal products.
